deviations.text: After the first jobs finished and before any verdict was computed, the analysis gained a list of timings whose median is more than twice their minimum, a count of records whose timing block held eight or fewer calls (a fixed cost of about 4 to 5.5 ms per block decides their median) and a sensitivity table that repeats every eager verdict with the minimum for those records. No threshold, cell, method or deciding statistic changed.
deviations.title: Suspect timings and short blocks

deviations.text: With power 2 and differentiate='params', the block layout of the projected bi-Laplacian held arrays made inside a jit trace and captured them in a custom_jvp rule, which raised 'No constant handler for type DynamicJaxprTracer' at min(D, H) >= 32. The constants are now numpy arrays turned into arrays where they are used; a regression test fails on the old code.
deviations.title: Planned bi-Laplacian gradient under jit at width 32 or more

deviations.text: jet_collapsed value-and-gradient failed on its second call (the module bakes parameter-dependent tensors); the PyTorch probe did not release a method's tensors, graphs and pools before the next method (out-of-memory records occurred with 75 to 79 GiB held); the PyTorch step baseline for jet_collapsed raised the same error and the nested-autograd step crashed the process at D = 1000. All fixed in the harness; every PyTorch job was rerun.
deviations.title: Second backward through a jet module, memory held between methods, training-step baselines

deviations.text: The timing protocol (nine blocks of about 30 ms, median), the cells, the methods, the seeds, the thresholds and the analysis rules are those registered; records with short blocks are not remeasured or removed.
deviations.title: What was not changed

deviations.text: The forced full stream engine stacks 4 D^2 + 1 channels at order four (262,145 at D = 256); its compile held more than 98 GiB of host memory for 40 minutes without finishing a cell. The order-four jobs were split: the first two cells with every method, the rest without the forced stream engines and the fused kernel.
deviations.title: Order-four jobs split

deviations.text: The first capture that ran out of memory left its pool allocated and every later capture of the process failed. The probe now skips a capture when too little memory is free (recorded as a missing device time) and resets a graph in a finally block. 333 of 1,229 PyTorch records still lack a device time because of the guard; the process holds far more reserved memory than its tensors need, and the larger part of that is not explained.
deviations.title: CUDA-graph capture memory on PyTorch

deviations.text: A failed capture left the default CUDA generator flagged as capturing, so the eager fallback and everything after it raised 'Offset increment outside graph capture encountered unexpectedly', and left the warm-up steps applied to the parameters. compile_training_step now abandons a failed capture: it resets the graph, renews the generator, restores parameters and optimizer state. A regression test fails on the old code.
deviations.title: Failed CUDA-graph capture in the PyTorch training step

deviations.text: With an unlimited memory budget the planner timed taylor_closed for Delta^2 above the size that compiles. taylor_closed is now refused for Delta^2 above 16,385 stacked channels (the largest size measured to compile), and the find timers of both back ends record a candidate that raised, out-of-memory included, as a failed candidate ranked last.
deviations.title: taylor_closed channel stall and find failures

deviations.text: The JAX probe built the exact rational polarization plan of the collapsed-Taylor baseline while listing methods, before the method filter; at order four and D = 256 it did not finish and held more than 150 GB of host memory. It is built on request and refused above D = 64 at order four, recorded as an error of that baseline.
deviations.title: Baseline plan built while listing methods

deviations.text: The method filter is a prefix match and did not select the forced candidates of the planner's pool, so no job ran them. They were run separately on PyTorch with the order-two cells; the run adds tables and no verdict.
deviations.title: Planner candidate pool not run

deviations.text: XLA crashed (segmentation fault) compiling a candidate it sized at 2.2 TB while the planned training method timed its pool under the registered unlimited budget (order four, D = 1024, B = 2048); the two cells at B = 2048 with D = 256 and 1024 were rerun with a 60 GiB budget for the planned methods, recorded in the protocol. A PyTorch process crashed once in the float32-TF32 candidate-pool job after 36 of 40 cells without a Python error; the last four cells were rerun.
deviations.title: Compiler crash on an unlimited memory budget; a TF32 pool crash

deviations.text: The planned training method spent more than 55 minutes timing candidates in the cell D = 256, B = 256 of order four; the unfinished cells were rerun as separate jobs with their own wall-clock limits, and the loaders merge the parts by cell.
deviations.title: Order-four cells after a stall

deviations.text: A job that measured the planned default in the cell D = 256, B = 256 of order four and then stalled for 72 minutes timing the planned training method's candidates was killed before the probe wrote the cell. The probe's method filter gained an exact-name form (an entry ending with `$`), and a separate job measured the planned default alone in that cell. The planned training method has no measurement there, from two jobs.
deviations.title: The planned default in one order-four cell
